correctness.rationale: Each induced-subgraph type is uniquely a multiset of maximal path-run lengths; left-to-right multiset permutations and stars-and-bars vacant-gap placements give precisely m_n(a). Its automorphism group is the product of a singleton-run symmetric group and hyperoctahedral wreath groups for longer runs. The map rho(s)=sum over restrictions is multiplicative: exactly the restrictions of st survive matched-source/range composition, and rho is unitriangular and invertible over all commutative unital rings. This gives the exact groupoid matrix blocks including the empty factor. Over C, symmetric-group and signed-wreath conjugacy classes are respectively partitions and bipartitions. Their multiplicative counts, followed by a minimum-slot constraint and formal Euler product, prove D_n. Independent direct enumerations n<=6, complete groupoid-basis pair-product tests n<=4, and coefficient checks n<=10 passed; beyond these ranges the all-n proof, not experimentation, supports the claim.

value.rationale: The natural target object is the complete semigroup algebra of PAut(P_n), and its matrix sizes, isotropy groups, and number of complex simple modules are intrinsic representation-theoretic invariants. The result gives the entire infinite family over arbitrary coefficient rings (not only small-case computation), plus an exact complex simple-module generating function with a nontrivial Euler product for symmetric and signed-wreath contributions. Such explicit data determine full characteristic-zero block multiplicities when combined with ordinary finite-group representation theory, whereas prior element counts do not. The contribution is stronger than a mere low-n table or routine recomputation of a known total.
